messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 (about 320 light‑years away) and has a mass of roughly 10 Jupiter masses and a radius of about 2.5 times that of Jupiter.  

Because it sits right on the boundary between massive planets and low‑mass brown dwarfs, some researchers classify it as a “super‑Jupiter” rather than a true planet.  Nonetheless, it remains the biggest object that astronomers have confidently identified as a planet in our current catalog.
